responsibility: This file implements GCC’s top-level compiler invocation workflow and the toplev class used by cc1-family executables. It owns much of the process-global compilation state, initializes diagnostics, options, plugins, timers, target/backend facilities, and language hooks, drives option processing and compilation of the main input, handles finalization and self-tests, emits version/help and patch-diff output, and provides cleanup so checking builds can re-enter portions of the compiler. Its responsibility is end-to-end orchestration of a compiler process rather than optimization logic for any specific IR.
same_name_distinction: This implementation file contains the actual top-level compiler process orchestration and defines much of the corresponding global state, including option storage, initialization/finalization flow, selftest handling, and the toplev method bodies. In contrast, gcc/toplev.h is the declaration surface exposing the toplev class, shared globals, and compiler-wide entry points to other files.
